ko.title: [소매 101 #5] 같은 우유 1갤런이 네 가지 다른 가격인 이유

segments.src: > Department stores, supercenters, convenience stores, and specialty shops aren't bigger and smaller versions of the same idea — they're four different answers to the question "what is the shopper standing here actually trying to do?"
segments.tr: > 백화점, 대형마트, 편의점, 전문점은 같은 개념의 큰 버전과 작은 버전이 아니다 — 이곳에 서 있는 고객이 실제로 하려는 것이 무엇인가에 대한 네 가지 다른 답이다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Retailers get sorted by **format** — the recurring bundle of choices a store makes about what it carries, how much help it gives you, and what it charges.
segments.tr: 소매업체는 **형식(format)**으로 분류된다 — 어떤 상품을 취급할지, 고객에게 얼마나 많은 도움을 줄지, 어떤 가격을 책정할지에 대한 정기적인 의사결정 묶음이다.

segments.src: Retailing textbooks (Levy & Weitz is the standard one) classify formats along four levers:
segments.tr: 소매 교과서(Levy & Weitz가 표준)는 형식을 네 가지 요소를 따라 분류한다:

segments.src: 1. **Variety** — how many different *categories* the store carries. Also called breadth. Milk, socks, motor oil, and a TV under one roof is high variety.
segments.tr: 1. **다양성(Variety)** — 매장이 취급하는 다양한 *카테고리*의 개수. 너비(breadth)라고도 불린다. 한 지붕 아래 우유, 양말, 모터 오일, TV를 모두 취급하는 것은 높은 다양성이다.

segments.src: 2. **Assortment** — how *deep* it goes inside one category. Also called depth. Forty running shoes in eleven widths is high assortment.
segments.tr: 2. **품목 다양성(Assortment)** — 한 카테고리 내에서 얼마나 *깊이* 있는지. 깊이(depth)라고도 불린다. 열한 가지 너비로 제공되는 40가지 러닝화는 높은 품목 다양성이다.

segments.src: 3. **Service level** — how much labor the store spends on you. Someone measuring your inseam is expensive; a self-checkout kiosk is not.
segments.tr: 3. **서비스 수준** — 매장이 고객을 위해 소비하는 노동력. 인심(inseam)을 측정해주는 사람은 비용이 많이 들고, 셀프 체크아웃 키오스크는 그렇지 않다.

segments.src: 4. **Price and margin** — what all of the above costs to run, and therefore what it costs you.
segments.tr: 4. **가격과 마진** — 위의 모든 것을 운영하는 데 드는 비용, 따라서 고객이 내는 비용이다.

segments.src: No store maxes out all four.
segments.tr: 어느 매장도 네 가지 모두에서 최고치를 달성하지는 못한다.

segments.src: That's the whole point.
segments.tr: 그것이 요점이다.

segments.src: Every format is a deliberate trade.
segments.tr: 모든 형식은 의도적인 거래다.

segments.src: **Department store** (Macy's, Nordstrom, Dillard's, Kohl's): high variety *and* decent depth, organized into walk-through departments — apparel, beauty, home, accessories.
segments.tr: **백화점** (Macy's, Nordstrom, Dillard's, Kohl's): 높은 다양성 *그리고* 적당한 깊이, 걷기 좋은 부서로 정렬 — 의류, 뷰티, 홈, 액세서리.

segments.src: High service, high margin, slow inventory turnover.
segments.tr: 높은 서비스, 높은 마진, 느린 재고 회전.

segments.src: Historically the format sold the *experience* of shopping as much as the goods.
segments.tr: 역사적으로 이 형식은 상품만큼 쇼핑의 *경험*을 팔았다.

segments.src: **The big box — supercenter and warehouse club** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): maximum variety, thin service, low price.
segments.tr: **대형점 — 슈퍼센터와 창고형 클럽** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): 최대한의 다양성, 얇은 서비스, 낮은 가격.

segments.src: A Walmart Supercenter runs roughly 180,000 square feet and stocks well over 100,000 items — general merchandise plus a full grocery.
segments.tr: Walmart Supercenter는 약 180,000제곱피트 규모로 100,000개가 넘는 상품을 취급한다 — 일반 상품과 완전한 식품점.

segments.src: A warehouse club goes the opposite way on depth: Costco deliberately carries only a few thousand items, one or two brands per need, sold in bulk from pallets, funded partly by an annual membership fee (about $65 for a basic card).
segments.tr: 창고형 클럽은 깊이 측면에서 반대 방향으로 간다: Costco는 의도적으로 수천 개 정도의 상품만 취급하고, 필요마다 한두 개 브랜드를 제공하며, 팰릿에서 대량으로 판매되고, 연간 회원비(기본 카드의 경우 약 $65)로 부분적으로 기금을 조달한다.

segments.src: Fewer choices → bigger orders per item → better cost from suppliers → lower shelf price.
segments.tr: 선택지 감소 → 상품당 더 큰 주문 → 공급자로부터의 더 나은 비용 → 더 낮은 선반 가격.

segments.src: **Convenience store** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): tiny variety, tiny depth, tiny footprint — typically around 2,500 square feet and a few thousand items.
segments.tr: **편의점** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): 작은 다양성, 작은 깊이, 작은 공간 — 일반적으로 약 2,500제곱피트 규모에 수천 개의 상품.

segments.src: What it actually sells is *time and proximity*.
segments.tr: 실제로 판매하는 것은 *시간과 근접성*이다.

segments.src: There are well over 100,000 of them in the U.S., a majority attached to fuel.
segments.tr: 미국에는 100,000개가 넘는 편의점이 있고, 대부분 연료 판매와 함께한다.

segments.src: Merchandise margins are high — roughly a third on in-store goods, far above a supermarket — because nobody price-shops a 90-second stop.
segments.tr: 상품 마진은 높다 — 점포 내 상품에서 대략 3분의 1로 슈퍼마켓보다 훨씬 높다 — 왜냐하면 아무도 90초짜리 정거소에서 가격을 비교하지 않기 때문이다.

segments.src: **Specialty store** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): narrow variety, extreme depth.
segments.tr: **전문점** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): 좁은 다양성, 극단적인 깊이.

segments.src: One category, done exhaustively, with staff who know it.
segments.tr: 한 카테고리를 철저하게 취급하고, 그것을 알고 있는 직원이 있다.

segments.src: When a specialty store gets big enough to dominate a category outright, it earns the nickname **category killer**.
segments.tr: 전문점이 카테고리를 완전히 지배할 정도로 충분히 커지면, **카테고리 킬러(category killer)**라는 별명을 얻는다.

segments.src: Underneath all four sits one arithmetic identity that explains most retail behavior:
segments.tr: 네 가지 모두의 기저에는 대부분의 소매 행동을 설명하는 하나의 산술 항등식이 있다:

segments.src: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover
segments.tr: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover

segments.src: You can win on fat margins and slow-moving goods (Nordstrom), or thin margins and goods that fly off the shelf (Costco, supermarkets).
segments.tr: 높은 마진과 천천히 팔리는 상품으로 승리할 수 있다 (Nordstrom), 또는 낮은 마진과 빠르게 팔리는 상품으로 승리할 수 있다 (Costco, 슈퍼마켓).

segments.src: What you cannot do is run thin margins on slow inventory.
segments.tr: 할 수 없는 것은 느린 재고에 낮은 마진을 운영하는 것이다.

segments.src: That combination is how chains die.
segments.tr: 그 조합이 체인점이 죽는 방식이다.

segments.src: One honest caveat: the boundaries leak.
segments.tr: 솔직한 한 가지 주의: 경계선이 흔들린다.

segments.src: Drugstores sell milk, supermarkets sell flowers, and c-stores sell hot pizza.
segments.tr: 약국은 우유를 판매하고, 슈퍼마켓은 꽃을 판매하고, 편의점은 핫 피자를 판매한다.

segments.src: The industry term for it is **scrambled merchandising** — formats grabbing categories outside their original lane in pursuit of turnover.
segments.tr: 이에 대한 업계 용어는 **혼합 판매(scrambled merchandising)** — 회전율을 추구하기 위해 형식이 원래의 영역 밖의 카테고리를 잡는 것이다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Follow one gallon of milk through a normal American week.
segments.tr: 일반적인 미국 주일 동안 1갤런의 우유를 따라가자.

segments.src: **Monday, 7:10 a.m.** You're already late.
segments.tr: **월요일, 오전 7시 10분** 이미 늦었다.

segments.src: You pull into the Circle K by the interstate ramp, grab coffee and a gallon, and you're back in the car in four minutes.
segments.tr: 고속도로 진출입로 옆 Circle K에 들어가서 커피와 1갤런을 집어 들고 4분 안에 다시 차에 탈 수 있다.

segments.src: Say it rings up around $5.29.
segments.tr: 약 $5.29가 나온다고 하자.

segments.src: You didn't compare anything.
segments.tr: 비교하지 않았다.

segments.src: You paid for the store being ninety seconds off your route and for a clerk being awake at 7 a.m.
segments.tr: 매장이 경로에서 90초 떨어져 있고, 직원이 오전 7시에 깨어 있는 것에 대해 돈을 냈다.

segments.src: **Saturday, 10 a.m.** Costco.
segments.tr: **토요일, 오전 10시** Costco.

segments.src: Two gallons banded together for roughly what one and a half cost on Monday, plus the $65 membership you already sank in January.
segments.tr: 월요일에 1.5갤런이 들던 비용 정도로 2갤런이 묶여 있고, 게다가 1월에 이미 투자한 $65 회원비가 있다.

segments.src: You walked past pallets, there were maybe two brands of milk, and you bagged nothing.
segments.tr: 팰릿을 지나 걸어가고, 우유 브랜드는 아마도 두 가지 정도가 있었고, 아무것도 포장하지 않았다.

segments.src: That's depth traded away for price.
segments.tr: 그것은 가격을 위해 거래된 깊이다.

segments.src: **Saturday, 11:30 a.m.** Target, because you also need socks, a floor lamp, a birthday card, and a prescription.
segments.tr: **토요일, 오전 11시 30분** Target, 왜냐하면 양말, 스탠드, 생일 카드, 처방약도 필요하기 때문이다.

segments.src: Milk here is somewhere between the other two.
segments.tr: 여기 우유는 다른 두 곳 사이 어딘가에 있다.

segments.src: You're not buying the cheapest milk — you're buying **one stop**.
segments.tr: 가장 저렴한 우유를 사는 것이 아니다 — **한 곳의 정거소**를 사는 것이다.

segments.src: Variety is the product.
segments.tr: 다양성이 상품이다.

segments.src: **Sunday afternoon.** Your cousin's wedding is in three weeks and you need a suit that fits.
segments.tr: **일요일 오후** 사촌의 결혼식이 3주 뒤에 있고 맞는 정장이 필요하다.

segments.src: You go to Nordstrom, a person puts a tape measure on you, marks the hem, and the store holds the jacket for a week.
segments.tr: Nordstrom에 가면, 직원이 줄자로 측정하고, 밑단을 표시하고, 매장이 재킷을 1주일간 보관한다.

segments.src: Nobody at Costco is doing that.
segments.tr: Costco의 아무도 그렇게 하지 않는다.

segments.src: You will pay for it in the price, and the store will hold that jacket in inventory for months before selling it.
segments.tr: 가격에 반영되어 비용을 내게 되고, 매장은 판매하기 전에 수개월 동안 재킷을 재고에 보관하게 된다.

segments.src: **Tuesday evening.** You want *good* trail runners.
segments.tr: **화요일 저녁** *좋은* 트레일 러닝화를 원한다.

segments.src: Not "shoes" — trail runners, for a specific arch.
segments.tr: "신발"이 아니라 — 특정 아치를 위한 트레일 러닝화.

segments.src: You go to a running specialty shop or REI, where one category fills the whole store and the person on the floor asks how many miles a week you run.
segments.tr: 러닝 전문점이나 REI에 가면, 한 카테고리가 전체 매장을 채우고, 현장의 직원이 주당 몇 마일을 달리는지 묻는다.

segments.src: Five errands, five formats, and every one of them was the right choice for the mission it served.
segments.tr: 다섯 가지 심부름, 다섯 가지 형식, 그리고 각각은 그것이 수행한 임무에 대해 올바른 선택이었다.

segments.src: Buying the suit at Costco or the emergency milk at Nordstrom would both be errors — the same kind of error, in opposite directions.
segments.tr: Costco에서 정장을 사거나 Nordstrom에서 긴급 우유를 사는 것은 모두 오류가 될 것이다 — 반대 방향의 같은 종류의 오류다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. A retail format is a bundle of four decisions — variety, assortment, service, and price — and no format wins on all four at once.
segments.tr: 1. 소매 형식은 네 가지 결정의 묶음이다 — 다양성, 품목 다양성, 서비스, 가격 — 그리고 어떤 형식도 네 가지 모두에서 동시에 승리하지는 못한다.

segments.src: 2. Department stores buy you breadth plus service, big boxes buy you breadth plus price, convenience stores buy you time, specialty stores buy you depth and expertise.
segments.tr: 2. 백화점은 너비와 서비스를 제공하고, 대형점은 너비와 가격을 제공하고, 편의점은 시간을 제공하고, 전문점은 깊이와 전문성을 제공한다.

segments.src: 3. Every one of them survives on the same equation — margin times turnover — and formats constantly poach categories from each other to keep the turnover side up.
segments.tr: 3. 그들 모두는 같은 공식으로 생존한다 — 마진 × 회전율 — 그리고 형식들은 회전율을 유지하기 위해 서로의 카테고리를 계속해서 빼앗아간다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 진단

segments.src: **Q1.** In retailing, "assortment" refers to which of the following?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 소매에서 "품목 다양성(assortment)"은 다음 중 무엇을 의미하는가?

segments.src: - (a) The total number of different product categories a store carries
segments.tr: - (a) 매장이 취급하는 다양한 상품 카테고리의 총 개수

segments.src: - (b) The depth of choices offered within a single category
segments.tr: - (b) 단일 카테고리 내에서 제공되는 선택지의 깊이

segments.src: - (c) The store's square footage
segments.tr: - (c) 매장의 제곱피트 면적

segments.src: - (d) The ratio of full-time to part-time staff
segments.tr: - (d) 정규직 대 비정규직 직원의 비율

segments.src: **Q2.** Costco carries only a few thousand items while a Walmart Supercenter carries well over 100,000.
segments.tr: **Q2.** Costco는 수천 개의 상품만 취급하는 반면 Walmart Supercenter는 100,000개가 넘는 상품을 취급한다.

segments.src: This mainly reflects a difference in strategy, not a failure by Costco.
segments.tr: 이것은 주로 전략의 차이를 반영하며, Costco의 실패가 아니다.

segments.src: (O / X)
segments.tr: (O / X)

segments.src: **Q3.** A convenience store charges more for the same gallon of milk than a supermarket does primarily because:
segments.tr: **Q3.** 편의점이 슈퍼마켓보다 같은 우유 1갤런에 더 많은 비용을 청구하는 주된 이유는:

segments.src: - (a) Its milk is a higher grade of product
segments.tr: - (a) 우유가 더 높은 등급의 상품이다

segments.src: - (b) It is legally required to price above supermarkets
segments.tr: - (b) 법적으로 슈퍼마켓보다 높게 가격을 매길 것을 요구받는다

segments.src: - (c) Its customers are buying proximity and speed, and its small scale carries higher cost per item sold
segments.tr: - (c) 고객들이 근접성과 속도를 사고 있으며, 작은 규모는 판매된 상품당 더 높은 비용을 초래한다

segments.src: - (d) It buys milk from different farms
segments.tr: - (d) 다른 농장에서 우유를 구매한다

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Retail format** — the recurring combination of variety, assortment, service level, and price that defines a type of store.
segments.tr: - **소매 형식** — 매장 유형을 정의하는 다양성, 품목 다양성, 서비스 수준, 가격의 반복적인 조합.

segments.src: - **Variety (breadth)** — how many distinct product categories a retailer carries.
segments.tr: - **다양성(Variety, 너비)** — 소매업체가 취급하는 서로 다른 상품 카테고리의 개수.

segments.src: - **Assortment (depth)** — how many choices — brands, sizes, styles — a retailer offers inside one category.
segments.tr: - **품목 다양성(Assortment, 깊이)** — 소매업체가 한 카테고리 내에서 제공하는 선택지의 개수 — 브랜드, 크기, 스타일.

segments.src: - **Scrambled merchandising** — a retailer adding categories outside its traditional lane, which blurs the lines between formats.
segments.tr: - **혼합 판매(Scrambled merchandising)** — 소매업체가 전통적인 영역 밖의 카테고리를 추가하여 형식 간의 경계를 흐릿하게 하는 것.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — how many times a year a retailer sells through and replaces its stock; the counterweight to gross margin.
segments.tr: - **재고 회전율(Inventory turnover)** — 소매업체가 연간 재고를 몇 번 판매하고 교체하는지; 총 마진의 상쇄.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** Assortment is depth within a category; breadth across categories is "variety."
segments.tr: *답변: **Q1 — (b).** 품목 다양성은 카테고리 내의 깊이이고, 카테고리 간의 너비는 "다양성"이다.

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Costco's limited item count is the mechanism of its low prices: fewer SKUs means larger orders per item, better supplier costs, and simpler operations.
segments.tr: **Q2 — O.** Costco의 제한된 상품 수는 낮은 가격의 메커니즘이다: 더 적은 SKU는 상품당 더 큰 주문, 더 나은 공급자 비용, 더 간단한 운영을 의미한다.

segments.src: **Q3 — (c).** The milk is the same product.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c).** 우유는 같은 상품이다.

segments.src: You are paying for location, hours, and speed, plus the higher per-item cost of running a 2,500-square-foot store — which is why in-store merchandise margins at convenience stores run far above supermarket levels.*

zh.title: [零售业101 #5] 为什么同一加仑牛奶有四种不同的价格

segments.src: > Department stores, supercenters, convenience stores, and specialty shops aren't bigger and smaller versions of the same idea — they're four different answers to the question "what is the shopper standing here actually trying to do?"
segments.tr: > 百货店、超级市场、便利店和专卖店不是同一概念的大小版本——它们是对"站在这里的购物者实际想做什么"这个问题的四种不同答案。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Retailers get sorted by **format** — the recurring bundle of choices a store makes about what it carries, how much help it gives you, and what it charges.
segments.tr: 零售商按**业态**分类——这是商店在经营商品、提供帮助程度和收费方面所做的反复出现的选择组合。

segments.src: Retailing textbooks (Levy & Weitz is the standard one) classify formats along four levers:
segments.tr: 零售教科书（Levy & Weitz是标准教材）沿四个维度对业态进行分类：

segments.src: 1. **Variety** — how many different *categories* the store carries. Also called breadth. Milk, socks, motor oil, and a TV under one roof is high variety.
segments.tr: 1. **品种广度** — 商店经营的不同*品类*的数量。也称为广度。牛奶、袜子、机油和电视在一个屋顶下是高品种广度。

segments.src: 2. **Assortment** — how *deep* it goes inside one category. Also called depth. Forty running shoes in eleven widths is high assortment.
segments.tr: 2. **品类深度** — 在一个品类内的深入程度。也称为深度。四十款跑鞋涵盖十一个宽度尺寸就是高品类深度。

segments.src: 3. **Service level** — how much labor the store spends on you. Someone measuring your inseam is expensive; a self-checkout kiosk is not.
segments.tr: 3. **服务水平** — 商店在你身上花费多少劳动力。有人为你量裤长很贵；自助结账亭则不是。

segments.src: 4. **Price and margin** — what all of the above costs to run, and therefore what it costs you.
segments.tr: 4. **价格和利润率** — 上述所有运营成本，因此也是你的成本。

segments.src: No store maxes out all four.
segments.tr: 没有商店在这四个方面都达到最高。

segments.src: That's the whole point.
segments.tr: 这就是关键所在。

segments.src: Every format is a deliberate trade.
segments.tr: 每种业态都是一种刻意的权衡。

segments.src: **Department store** (Macy's, Nordstrom, Dillard's, Kohl's): high variety *and* decent depth, organized into walk-through departments — apparel, beauty, home, accessories.
segments.tr: **百货店**（梅西百货、诺德斯特龙、迪拉德百货、科尔百货）：品种广泛*且*品类较深，组织成可行走的部门——服装、美妆、家居、配饰。

segments.src: High service, high margin, slow inventory turnover.
segments.tr: 高服务、高利润率、库存周转缓慢。

segments.src: Historically the format sold the *experience* of shopping as much as the goods.
segments.tr: 从历史上看，这种业态销售的是购物的*体验*与商品本身一样多。

segments.src: **The big box — supercenter and warehouse club** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): maximum variety, thin service, low price.
segments.tr: **大型零售商——超级市场和仓储俱乐部**（沃尔玛超级市场、Target、Meijer；Costco、山姆会员店、BJ会员店）：品种最多、服务简洁、价格低廉。

segments.src: A Walmart Supercenter runs roughly 180,000 square feet and stocks well over 100,000 items — general merchandise plus a full grocery.
segments.tr: 沃尔玛超级市场大约有180,000平方英尺，库存超过100,000件商品——日用品加全面的杂货。

segments.src: A warehouse club goes the opposite way on depth: Costco deliberately carries only a few thousand items, one or two brands per need, sold in bulk from pallets, funded partly by an annual membership fee (about $65 for a basic card).
segments.tr: 仓储俱乐部在深度上采取相反的方式：Costco有意只经营几千种商品，每项需求只有一两个品牌，从托盘上以散装形式销售，部分由年度会员费（基本卡约$65）提供资金。

segments.src: Fewer choices → bigger orders per item → better cost from suppliers → lower shelf price.
segments.tr: 更少的选择 → 每件更大的订单 → 从供应商获得更低的成本 → 更低的架上价格。

segments.src: **Convenience store** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): tiny variety, tiny depth, tiny footprint — typically around 2,500 square feet and a few thousand items.
segments.tr: **便利店**（7-Eleven、Wawa、QuikTrip、Circle K）：品种极少、品类浅、占地面积小——通常约2,500平方英尺和几千种商品。

segments.src: What it actually sells is *time and proximity*.
segments.tr: 它实际销售的是*时间和便利性*。

segments.src: There are well over 100,000 of them in the U.S., a majority attached to fuel.
segments.tr: 美国有10万多家，其中大多数附带加油站。

segments.src: Merchandise margins are high — roughly a third on in-store goods, far above a supermarket — because nobody price-shops a 90-second stop.
segments.tr: 商品利润率很高——店内商品大约三分之一，远高于超市——因为没人会在90秒的快速停留中货比三家。

segments.src: **Specialty store** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): narrow variety, extreme depth.
segments.tr: **专卖店**（丝芙兰、Foot Locker、REI、百思买、家得宝）：品种单一、品类极深。

segments.src: One category, done exhaustively, with staff who know it.
segments.tr: 一个品类，做得面面俱到，员工懂行。

segments.src: When a specialty store gets big enough to dominate a category outright, it earns the nickname **category killer**.
segments.tr: 当专卖店足够大到彻底主导一个品类时，它赢得了**品类杀手**的绰号。

segments.src: Underneath all four sits one arithmetic identity that explains most retail behavior:
segments.tr: 在这四种业态的底层，有一个算术恒等式解释了大多数零售行为：

segments.src: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover
segments.tr: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover

segments.src: You can win on fat margins and slow-moving goods (Nordstrom), or thin margins and goods that fly off the shelf (Costco, supermarkets).
segments.tr: 你可以通过厚利润和缓慢流动的商品获胜（诺德斯特龙），或者通过薄利润和快速流动的商品获胜（Costco、超市）。

segments.src: What you cannot do is run thin margins on slow inventory.
segments.tr: 你不能做的是以低利润运营缓慢库存。

segments.src: That combination is how chains die.
segments.tr: 这种组合是连锁店死亡的方式。

segments.src: One honest caveat: the boundaries leak.
segments.tr: 一个诚实的警告：边界会泄漏。

segments.src: Drugstores sell milk, supermarkets sell flowers, and c-stores sell hot pizza.
segments.tr: 药店卖牛奶，超市卖花，便利店卖热比萨。

segments.src: The industry term for it is **scrambled merchandising** — formats grabbing categories outside their original lane in pursuit of turnover.
segments.tr: 业界称之为**混合商品销售**——业态为了追求周转率而抓住原本范围外的品类。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Follow one gallon of milk through a normal American week.
segments.tr: 跟踪一加仑牛奶在正常美国一周内的情况。

segments.src: **Monday, 7:10 a.m.** You're already late.
segments.tr: **周一，上午7:10** 你已经迟到了。

segments.src: You pull into the Circle K by the interstate ramp, grab coffee and a gallon, and you're back in the car in four minutes.
segments.tr: 你拉进州际公路匝道旁的Circle K便利店，抓起咖啡和一加仑牛奶，四分钟内回到车上。

segments.src: Say it rings up around $5.29.
segments.tr: 假设它的结账价格约为$5.29。

segments.src: You didn't compare anything.
segments.tr: 你没有比较任何东西。

segments.src: You paid for the store being ninety seconds off your route and for a clerk being awake at 7 a.m.
segments.tr: 你为商店距离你的路线只有90秒钟和店员早上7点还在班付费。

segments.src: **Saturday, 10 a.m.** Costco.
segments.tr: **周六，上午10点** Costco。

segments.src: Two gallons banded together for roughly what one and a half cost on Monday, plus the $65 membership you already sank in January.
segments.tr: 两加仑捆在一起的价格大约是周一一加半的价格，加上你在1月已经花费的$65会员费。

segments.src: You walked past pallets, there were maybe two brands of milk, and you bagged nothing.
segments.tr: 你经过了托盘，也许只有两个牛奶品牌，你没有打包任何东西。

segments.src: That's depth traded away for price.
segments.tr: 这是为了价格而放弃的深度。

segments.src: **Saturday, 11:30 a.m.** Target, because you also need socks, a floor lamp, a birthday card, and a prescription.
segments.tr: **周六，上午11:30** Target，因为你还需要袜子、落地灯、生日卡和处方。

segments.src: Milk here is somewhere between the other two.
segments.tr: 这里的牛奶介于其他两者之间。

segments.src: You're not buying the cheapest milk — you're buying **one stop**.
segments.tr: 你买的不是最便宜的牛奶——你买的是**一次购物**。

segments.src: Variety is the product.
segments.tr: 品种广度是产品。

segments.src: **Sunday afternoon.** Your cousin's wedding is in three weeks and you need a suit that fits.
segments.tr: **周日下午** 你表哥的婚礼在三周后，你需要一套合身的西装。

segments.src: You go to Nordstrom, a person puts a tape measure on you, marks the hem, and the store holds the jacket for a week.
segments.tr: 你去诺德斯特龙，一个人给你量体，标记裤脚，商店为你保留一周的夹克。

segments.src: Nobody at Costco is doing that.
segments.tr: Costco没有人这样做。

segments.src: You will pay for it in the price, and the store will hold that jacket in inventory for months before selling it.
segments.tr: 你会在价格中为此付费，商店会将该夹克保留在库存中数月才能售出。

segments.src: **Tuesday evening.** You want *good* trail runners.
segments.tr: **周二晚上** 你想要*好的*越野跑鞋。

segments.src: Not "shoes" — trail runners, for a specific arch.
segments.tr: 不是"鞋"——越野跑鞋，针对特定的足弓。

segments.src: You go to a running specialty shop or REI, where one category fills the whole store and the person on the floor asks how many miles a week you run.
segments.tr: 你去跑步专卖店或REI，那里一个品类填满了整个店铺，地板上的人会问你一周跑多少英里。

segments.src: Five errands, five formats, and every one of them was the right choice for the mission it served.
segments.tr: 五个差事，五种业态，每一个都是为其服务的任务的正确选择。

segments.src: Buying the suit at Costco or the emergency milk at Nordstrom would both be errors — the same kind of error, in opposite directions.
segments.tr: 在Costco买西装或在诺德斯特龙买应急牛奶都是错误——同样的错误，方向相反。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. A retail format is a bundle of four decisions — variety, assortment, service, and price — and no format wins on all four at once.
segments.tr: 1. 零售业态是四个决策的组合——品种广度、品类深度、服务和价格——没有哪种业态在这四个方面都同时胜出。

segments.src: 2. Department stores buy you breadth plus service, big boxes buy you breadth plus price, convenience stores buy you time, specialty stores buy you depth and expertise.
segments.tr: 2. 百货店为你提供广度加服务，大型零售商为你提供广度加价格，便利店为你提供时间，专卖店为你提供深度和专业知识。

segments.src: 3. Every one of them survives on the same equation — margin times turnover — and formats constantly poach categories from each other to keep the turnover side up.
segments.tr: 3. 它们都依靠同一个公式生存——利润率乘以周转率——各业态不断从彼此那里抢夺品类以保持周转率的上升。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自我测验

segments.src: **Q1.** In retailing, "assortment" refers to which of the following?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 在零售业中，"品类深度"指的是以下哪一项？

segments.src: - (a) The total number of different product categories a store carries
segments.tr: - (a) 商店经营的不同产品品类的总数

segments.src: - (b) The depth of choices offered within a single category
segments.tr: - (b) 在单个品类内提供的选择深度

segments.src: - (c) The store's square footage
segments.tr: - (c) 商店的平方英尺数

segments.src: - (d) The ratio of full-time to part-time staff
segments.tr: - (d) 全职员工与兼职员工的比例

segments.src: **Q2.** Costco carries only a few thousand items while a Walmart Supercenter carries well over 100,000.
segments.tr: **Q2.** Costco只经营几千种商品，而沃尔玛超级市场经营超过100,000种。

segments.src: This mainly reflects a difference in strategy, not a failure by Costco.
segments.tr: 这主要反映了战略上的差异，而不是Costco的失败。

segments.src: (O / X)
segments.tr: (O / X)

segments.src: **Q3.** A convenience store charges more for the same gallon of milk than a supermarket does primarily because:
segments.tr: **Q3.** 便利店对同一加仑牛奶的收费比超市高，主要是因为：

segments.src: - (a) Its milk is a higher grade of product
segments.tr: - (a) 它的牛奶是更高级的产品

segments.src: - (b) It is legally required to price above supermarkets
segments.tr: - (b) 法律要求它的价格高于超市

segments.src: - (c) Its customers are buying proximity and speed, and its small scale carries higher cost per item sold
segments.tr: - (c) 它的顾客购买的是便利和速度，其小规模导致每件商品的销售成本更高

segments.src: - (d) It buys milk from different farms
segments.tr: - (d) 它从不同的农场购买牛奶

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今天的术语

segments.src: - **Retail format** — the recurring combination of variety, assortment, service level, and price that defines a type of store.
segments.tr: - **零售业态** — 定义商店类型的品种广度、品类深度、服务水平和价格的反复出现的组合。

segments.src: - **Variety (breadth)** — how many distinct product categories a retailer carries.
segments.tr: - **品种广度** — 零售商经营多少种不同的产品品类。

segments.src: - **Assortment (depth)** — how many choices — brands, sizes, styles — a retailer offers inside one category.
segments.tr: - **品类深度** — 零售商在一个品类内提供多少选择——品牌、尺寸、款式。

segments.src: - **Scrambled merchandising** — a retailer adding categories outside its traditional lane, which blurs the lines between formats.
segments.tr: - **混合商品销售** — 零售商增加传统范围外的品类，这模糊了业态之间的界限。

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — how many times a year a retailer sells through and replaces its stock; the counterweight to gross margin.
segments.tr: - **库存周转率** — 零售商每年销售完整及替换库存的次数；与毛利率的平衡。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** Assortment is depth within a category; breadth across categories is "variety."
segments.tr: *答案：**Q1 — (b).** 品类深度是品类内的深度；跨品类的广度是"品种广度"。

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Costco's limited item count is the mechanism of its low prices: fewer SKUs means larger orders per item, better supplier costs, and simpler operations.
segments.tr: **Q2 — O.** Costco的有限商品数量是其低价的机制：更少的SKU意味着每件更大的订单、更好的供应商成本和更简单的运营。

segments.src: **Q3 — (c).** The milk is the same product.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c).** 牛奶是相同的产品。

segments.src: You are paying for location, hours, and speed, plus the higher per-item cost of running a 2,500-square-foot store — which is why in-store merchandise margins at convenience stores run far above supermarket levels.*
segments.tr: 你为位置、营业时间和速度付费，加上运营2,500平方英尺商店的更高的单件成本——这就是为什么便利店的店内商品利润率远高于超市水平。*

hi.title: [रिटेलिंग 101 #5] एक ही गैलन दूध की कीमत चार अलग-अलग कीमतों पर क्यों है

segments.src: > Department stores, supercenters, convenience stores, and specialty shops aren't bigger and smaller versions of the same idea — they're four different answers to the question "what is the shopper standing here actually trying to do?"
segments.tr: > डिपार्टमेंट स्टोर, सुपरसेंटर, सुविधा स्टोर और विशेषता दुकानें एक ही विचार के बड़े और छोटे संस्करण नहीं हैं — वे इस सवाल के चार अलग-अलग जवाब हैं "यहां खड़ा खरीदार वास्तव में क्या करने की कोशिश कर रहा है?"

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Retailers get sorted by **format** — the recurring bundle of choices a store makes about what it carries, how much help it gives you, and what it charges.
segments.tr: खुदरा विक्रेताओं को **प्रारूप** द्वारा वर्गीकृत किया जाता है — विकल्पों का एक आवर्ती बंडल जो एक स्टोर क्या ले जाता है, वह आपको कितनी मदद देता है, और वह आपसे क्या शुल्क लेता है, इसके बारे में बनाता है।

segments.src: Retailing textbooks (Levy & Weitz is the standard one) classify formats along four levers:
segments.tr: खुदरा पाठ्यपुस्तकें (लेवी और वीट्ज़ मानक है) चार लीवर के साथ प्रारूपों को वर्गीकृत करती हैं:

segments.src: 1. **Variety** — how many different *categories* the store carries. Also called breadth. Milk, socks, motor oil, and a TV under one roof is high variety.
segments.tr: 1. **विविधता** — स्टोर कितनी अलग-अलग *श्रेणियां* ले जाता है। चौड़ाई भी कहा जाता है। दूध, मोजे, मोटर ऑयल, और एक टीवी एक छत के नीचे उच्च विविधता है।

segments.src: 2. **Assortment** — how *deep* it goes inside one category. Also called depth. Forty running shoes in eleven widths is high assortment.
segments.tr: 2. **संग्रह** — यह एक श्रेणी के अंदर कितना *गहरा* जाता है। गहराई भी कहा जाता है। ग्यारह चौड़ाई में चालीस दौड़ने वाले जूते उच्च संग्रह हैं।

segments.src: 3. **Service level** — how much labor the store spends on you. Someone measuring your inseam is expensive; a self-checkout kiosk is not.
segments.tr: 3. **सेवा स्तर** — स्टोर आपके लिए कितनी मेहनत करता है। आपके इनसीम को मापने वाला कोई महंगा है; एक सेल्फ-चेकआउट कियोस्क नहीं है।

segments.src: 4. **Price and margin** — what all of the above costs to run, and therefore what it costs you.
segments.tr: 4. **कीमत और मार्जिन** — उपरोक्त सभी को चलाने में क्या खर्च होता है, और इसलिए यह आपको क्या खर्च होता है।

segments.src: No store maxes out all four.
segments.tr: कोई स्टोर चारों को अधिकतम नहीं करता है।

segments.src: That's the whole point.
segments.tr: यह पूरा बिंदु है।

segments.src: Every format is a deliberate trade.
segments.tr: हर प्रारूप एक जानबूझकर व्यापार है।

segments.src: **Department store** (Macy's, Nordstrom, Dillard's, Kohl's): high variety *and* decent depth, organized into walk-through departments — apparel, beauty, home, accessories.
segments.tr: **डिपार्टमेंट स्टोर** (मेसीज़, नॉर्डस्ट्रॉम, डिलार्ड्स, कोहल्स): उच्च विविधता *और* अच्छी गहराई, वॉक-थ्रू विभागों में संगठित — परिधान, सौंदर्य, घर, सहायक उपकरण।

segments.src: High service, high margin, slow inventory turnover.
segments.tr: उच्च सेवा, उच्च मार्जिन, धीमी सूची टर्नओवर।

segments.src: Historically the format sold the *experience* of shopping as much as the goods.
segments.tr: ऐतिहासिक रूप से प्रारूप ने खरीदारी के *अनुभव* को माल के रूप में बेचा।

segments.src: **The big box — supercenter and warehouse club** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): maximum variety, thin service, low price.
segments.tr: **बड़ा बॉक्स — सुपरसेंटर और वेयरहाउस क्लब** (वालमार्ट सुपरसेंटर, टार्गेट, मेजर; कॉस्टको, सैम्स क्लब, बीजे): अधिकतम विविधता, पतली सेवा, कम कीमत।

segments.src: A Walmart Supercenter runs roughly 180,000 square feet and stocks well over 100,000 items — general merchandise plus a full grocery.
segments.tr: एक वालमार्ट सुपरसेंटर लगभग 180,000 वर्ग फीट चलाता है और 100,000 से अधिक वस्तुओं का स्टॉक करता है — सामान्य माल और साथ ही पूर्ण किराना।

segments.src: A warehouse club goes the opposite way on depth: Costco deliberately carries only a few thousand items, one or two brands per need, sold in bulk from pallets, funded partly by an annual membership fee (about $65 for a basic card).
segments.tr: एक वेयरहाउस क्लब गहराई के विपरीत तरीके से जाता है: कॉस्टको जानबूझकर केवल कुछ हजार वस्तुओं को ले जाता है, प्रति आवश्यकता एक या दो ब्रांड, पैलेट से थोक में बेचा जाता है, आंशिक रूप से एक वार्षिक सदस्यता शुल्क द्वारा वित्त पोषित (एक बुनियादी कार्ड के लिए लगभग $65)।

segments.src: Fewer choices → bigger orders per item → better cost from suppliers → lower shelf price.
segments.tr: कम विकल्प → प्रति वस्तु बड़े आदेश → आपूर्तिकर्ताओं से बेहतर लागत → कम अलमारी मूल्य।

segments.src: **Convenience store** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): tiny variety, tiny depth, tiny footprint — typically around 2,500 square feet and a few thousand items.
segments.tr: **सुविधा स्टोर** (7-इलेवन, वावा, क्विकट्रिप, सर्कल के): छोटी विविधता, छोटी गहराई, छोटा पदचिह्न — आमतौर पर लगभग 2,500 वर्ग फीट और कुछ हजार वस्तुएं।

segments.src: What it actually sells is *time and proximity*.
segments.tr: यह वास्तव में क्या बेचता है वह *समय और निकटता* है।

segments.src: There are well over 100,000 of them in the U.S., a majority attached to fuel.
segments.tr: अमेरिका में 100,000 से अधिक हैं, बहुमत ईंधन से जुड़े हुए हैं।

segments.src: Merchandise margins are high — roughly a third on in-store goods, far above a supermarket — because nobody price-shops a 90-second stop.
segments.tr: वस्तु मार्जिन अधिक हैं — इन-स्टोर सामानों पर लगभग एक तिहाई, सुपरमार्केट से बहुत ऊपर — क्योंकि कोई भी 90 सेकंड के स्टॉप पर कीमत नहीं खरीदता है।

segments.src: **Specialty store** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): narrow variety, extreme depth.
segments.tr: **विशेषता स्टोर** (सेफोरा, फुट लॉकर, आरईआई, बेस्ट बाय, होम डिपो): संकीर्ण विविधता, चरम गहराई।

segments.src: One category, done exhaustively, with staff who know it.
segments.tr: एक श्रेणी, संपूर्ण रूप से की गई, कर्मचारियों के साथ जो इसे जानते हैं।

segments.src: When a specialty store gets big enough to dominate a category outright, it earns the nickname **category killer**.
segments.tr: जब एक विशेषता स्टोर एक श्रेणी पर पूरी तरह हावी होने के लिए काफी बड़ा हो जाता है, तो इसे **श्रेणी हत्यारा** का उपनाम मिलता है।

segments.src: Underneath all four sits one arithmetic identity that explains most retail behavior:
segments.tr: चारों के नीचे एक अंकगणितीय पहचान बैठती है जो अधिकांश खुदरा व्यवहार की व्याख्या करती है:

segments.src: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover
segments.tr: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover

segments.src: You can win on fat margins and slow-moving goods (Nordstrom), or thin margins and goods that fly off the shelf (Costco, supermarkets).
segments.tr: आप मोटे मार्जिन और धीमी गति वाली वस्तुओं (नॉर्डस्ट्रॉम) पर जीत सकते हैं, या पतले मार्जिन और वस्तुएं जो अलमारी से उड़ जाती हैं (कॉस्टको, सुपरमार्केट)।

segments.src: What you cannot do is run thin margins on slow inventory.
segments.tr: आप जो नहीं कर सकते वह धीमी सूची पर पतले मार्जिन चलाना है।

segments.src: That combination is how chains die.
segments.tr: वह संयोजन यह है कि श्रृंखलाएं कैसे मरती हैं।

segments.src: One honest caveat: the boundaries leak.
segments.tr: एक ईमानदार चेतावनी: सीमाएं रिसती हैं।

segments.src: Drugstores sell milk, supermarkets sell flowers, and c-stores sell hot pizza.
segments.tr: ड्रग स्टोर दूध बेचते हैं, सुपरमार्केट फूल बेचते हैं, और सी-स्टोर गर्म पिज्जा बेचते हैं।

segments.src: The industry term for it is **scrambled merchandising** — formats grabbing categories outside their original lane in pursuit of turnover.
segments.tr: इसके लिए उद्योग शब्द **उलझे हुए व्यापार** है — टर्नओवर की खोज में अपने मूल लेन के बाहर की श्रेणियों को पकड़ने वाले प्रारूप।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Follow one gallon of milk through a normal American week.
segments.tr: एक सामान्य अमेरिकी सप्ताह में दूध के एक गैलन का पालन करें।

segments.src: **Monday, 7:10 a.m.** You're already late.
segments.tr: **सोमवार, 7:10 पूर्वाह्न** आप पहले से ही देर हो चुके हैं।

segments.src: You pull into the Circle K by the interstate ramp, grab coffee and a gallon, and you're back in the car in four minutes.
segments.tr: आप राजमार्ग रैंप के बगल में सर्कल के में खींचते हैं, कॉफी और एक गैलन लेते हैं, और आप चार मिनट में कार में वापस आ जाते हैं।

segments.src: Say it rings up around $5.29.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए यह लगभग $5.29 तक बजता है।

segments.src: You didn't compare anything.
segments.tr: आपने कुछ भी तुलना नहीं की।

segments.src: You paid for the store being ninety seconds off your route and for a clerk being awake at 7 a.m.
segments.tr: आपने स्टोर के लिए आपके रूट से नब्बे सेकंड दूर होने के लिए भुगतान किया और एक क्लर्क सुबह 7 बजे जागने के लिए।

segments.src: **Saturday, 10 a.m.** Costco.
segments.tr: **शनिवार, सुबह 10 बजे** कॉस्टको।

segments.src: Two gallons banded together for roughly what one and a half cost on Monday, plus the $65 membership you already sank in January.
segments.tr: दो गैलन एक साथ बंधे हुए हैं जो सोमवार को लगभग डेढ़ की लागत के लिए, साथ ही $65 सदस्यता जो आपने पहले ही जनवरी में डूबा दिया।

segments.src: You walked past pallets, there were maybe two brands of milk, and you bagged nothing.
segments.tr: आप पैलेट के पास चले गए, शायद दूध की दो ब्रांड थीं, और आपने कुछ भी बैग नहीं किया।

segments.src: That's depth traded away for price.
segments.tr: यह कीमत के लिए व्यापार किए गई गहराई है।

segments.src: **Saturday, 11:30 a.m.** Target, because you also need socks, a floor lamp, a birthday card, and a prescription.
segments.tr: **शनिवार, 11:30 पूर्वाह्न** लक्ष्य, क्योंकि आपको मोजे, एक फर्श दीपक, एक जन्मदिन का कार्ड और एक नुस्खे की भी आवश्यकता है।

segments.src: Milk here is somewhere between the other two.
segments.tr: यहां दूध दूसरे दोनों के बीच कहीं है।

segments.src: You're not buying the cheapest milk — you're buying **one stop**.
segments.tr: आप सबसे सस्ता दूध नहीं खरीद रहे हैं — आप **एक स्टॉप** खरीद रहे हैं।

segments.src: Variety is the product.
segments.tr: विविधता उत्पाद है।

segments.src: **Sunday afternoon.** Your cousin's wedding is in three weeks and you need a suit that fits.
segments.tr: **रविवार दोपहर।** आपके चचेरे भाई की शादी तीन सप्ताह में है और आपको एक सूट की आवश्यकता है जो फिट हो।

segments.src: You go to Nordstrom, a person puts a tape measure on you, marks the hem, and the store holds the jacket for a week.
segments.tr: आप नॉर्डस्ट्रॉम जाते हैं, एक व्यक्ति आपको टेप का माप देता है, hem को चिह्नित करता है, और स्टोर एक सप्ताह के लिए जैकेट को पकड़ता है।

segments.src: Nobody at Costco is doing that.
segments.tr: कॉस्टको में कोई भी ऐसा नहीं कर रहा है।

segments.src: You will pay for it in the price, and the store will hold that jacket in inventory for months before selling it.
segments.tr: आप कीमत में इसके लिए भुगतान करेंगे, और स्टोर बेचने से पहले महीनों के लिए सूची में जैकेट को रखेगा।

segments.src: **Tuesday evening.** You want *good* trail runners.
segments.tr: **मंगलवार की शाम।** आप *अच्छे* ट्रेल धावक चाहते हैं।

segments.src: Not "shoes" — trail runners, for a specific arch.
segments.tr: "जूते" नहीं — ट्रेल धावक, एक विशिष्ट मेहराब के लिए।

segments.src: You go to a running specialty shop or REI, where one category fills the whole store and the person on the floor asks how many miles a week you run.
segments.tr: आप एक दौड़ने विशेषता की दुकान या आरईआई जाते हैं, जहां एक श्रेणी पूरे स्टोर को भरती है और फर्श पर व्यक्ति पूछता है कि आप एक सप्ताह में कितने मील दौड़ते हैं।

segments.src: Five errands, five formats, and every one of them was the right choice for the mission it served.
segments.tr: पांच काम, पांच प्रारूप, और उनमें से प्रत्येक इसकी सेवा करने वाले मिशन के लिए सही विकल्प था।

segments.src: Buying the suit at Costco or the emergency milk at Nordstrom would both be errors — the same kind of error, in opposite directions.
segments.tr: कॉस्टको में सूट खरीदना या नॉर्डस्ट्रॉम में आपातकालीन दूध दोनों त्रुटियां होंगी — एक ही प्रकार की त्रुटि, विपरीत दिशाओं में।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-लाइन पुनरावृत्ति

segments.src: 1. A retail format is a bundle of four decisions — variety, assortment, service, and price — and no format wins on all four at once.
segments.tr: 1. एक खुदरा प्रारूप चार निर्णयों का एक बंडल है — विविधता, संग्रह, सेवा, और कीमत — और कोई भी प्रारूप एक साथ सभी चार पर नहीं जीतता है।

segments.src: 2. Department stores buy you breadth plus service, big boxes buy you breadth plus price, convenience stores buy you time, specialty stores buy you depth and expertise.
segments.tr: 2. डिपार्टमेंट स्टोर आपको चौड़ाई जमा सेवा खरीदते हैं, बड़े बॉक्स आपको चौड़ाई जमा कीमत खरीदते हैं, सुविधा स्टोर आपको समय खरीदते हैं, विशेषता स्टोर आपको गहराई और विशेषज्ञता खरीदते हैं।

segments.src: 3. Every one of them survives on the same equation — margin times turnover — and formats constantly poach categories from each other to keep the turnover side up.
segments.tr: 3. उनमें से प्रत्येक एक ही समीकरण पर जीवित रहता है — मार्जिन बार टर्नओवर — और प्रारूप लगातार एक दूसरे से श्रेणियों को पकड़ते हैं ताकि टर्नओवर पक्ष को ऊपर रखा जा सके।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ आत्म-क्विज़

segments.src: **Q1.** In retailing, "assortment" refers to which of the following?
segments.tr: **प्रश्न 1।** खुदरा में, "संग्रह" निम्नलिखित में से किसे संदर्भित करता है?

segments.src: - (a) The total number of different product categories a store carries
segments.tr: - (a) एक स्टोर जो विभिन्न पणय श्रेणियों की कुल संख्या है

segments.src: - (b) The depth of choices offered within a single category
segments.tr: - (b) एक एकल श्रेणी के भीतर पेश किए गए विकल्पों की गहराई

segments.src: - (c) The store's square footage
segments.tr: - (c) स्टोर का वर्ग फुटेज

segments.src: - (d) The ratio of full-time to part-time staff
segments.tr: - (d) पूर्ण समय से अंशकालीन कर्मचारियों का अनुपात

segments.src: **Q2.** Costco carries only a few thousand items while a Walmart Supercenter carries well over 100,000.
segments.tr: **प्रश्न 2।** कॉस्टको केवल कुछ हजार वस्तुओं को ले जाता है जबकि वालमार्ट सुपरसेंटर 100,000 से अधिक ले जाता है।

segments.src: This mainly reflects a difference in strategy, not a failure by Costco.
segments.tr: यह मुख्य रूप से रणनीति में एक अंतर को दर्शाता है, कॉस्टको की विफलता नहीं।

segments.src: (O / X)
**Q3.** A convenience store charges more for the same gallon of milk than a supermarket does primarily because:
segments.tr: **प्रश्न 3।** एक सुविधा स्टोर दूध के समान गैलन के लिए सुपरमार्केट की तुलना में अधिक शुल्क लेता है मुख्य रूप से क्योंकि:

segments.src: - (a) Its milk is a higher grade of product
segments.tr: - (a) इसका दूध एक उच्च श्रेणी का उत्पाद है

segments.src: - (b) It is legally required to price above supermarkets
segments.tr: - (b) यह कानूनी रूप से सुपरमार्केट के ऊपर कीमत के लिए आवश्यक है

segments.src: - (c) Its customers are buying proximity and speed, and its small scale carries higher cost per item sold
segments.tr: - (c) इसके ग्राहक निकटता और गति खरीद रहे हैं, और इसके छोटे पैमाने पर बेची गई प्रति वस्तु उच्च लागत है

segments.src: - (d) It buys milk from different farms
segments.tr: - (d) यह विभिन्न खेतों से दूध खरीदता है

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Retail format** — the recurring combination of variety, assortment, service level, and price that defines a type of store.
segments.tr: - **खुदरा प्रारूप** — विविधता, संग्रह, सेवा स्तर और कीमत का आवर्ती संयोजन जो एक स्टोर के प्रकार को परिभाषित करता है।

segments.src: - **Variety (breadth)** — how many distinct product categories a retailer carries.
segments.tr: - **विविधता (चौड़ाई)** — एक खुदरा विक्रेता कितनी अलग-अलग पणय श्रेणियों को ले जाता है।

segments.src: - **Assortment (depth)** — how many choices — brands, sizes, styles — a retailer offers inside one category.
segments.tr: - **संग्रह (गहराई)** — कितने विकल्प — ब्रांड, आकार, शैलियां — एक खुदरा विक्रेता एक श्रेणी के अंदर प्रदान करता है।

segments.src: - **Scrambled merchandising** — a retailer adding categories outside its traditional lane, which blurs the lines between formats.

es.title: [Minorismo 101 #5] Por Qué el Mismo Galón de Leche Cuesta Cuatro Precios Diferentes

segments.src: > Department stores, supercenters, convenience stores, and specialty shops aren't bigger and smaller versions of the same idea — they're four different answers to the question "what is the shopper standing here actually trying to do?"
segments.tr: > Las tiendas departamentales, supermercados, tiendas de conveniencia y tiendas especializadas no son versiones más grandes y más pequeñas de la misma idea — son cuatro respuestas diferentes a la pregunta "¿qué intenta hacer realmente el cliente que está aquí?"

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Retailers get sorted by **format** — the recurring bundle of choices a store makes about what it carries, how much help it gives you, and what it charges.
segments.tr: Los minoristas se clasifican por **formato** — el conjunto recurrente de decisiones que una tienda toma sobre qué vende, cuánta ayuda te proporciona y cuánto cobra.

segments.src: Retailing textbooks (Levy & Weitz is the standard one) classify formats along four levers:
segments.tr: Los libros de texto sobre minorismo (Levy & Weitz es el estándar) clasifican los formatos a través de cuatro palancas:

segments.src: 1. **Variety** — how many different *categories* the store carries. Also called breadth. Milk, socks, motor oil, and a TV under one roof is high variety.
segments.tr: 1. **Variedad** — cuántas *categorías* diferentes vende la tienda. También llamada amplitud. Leche, calcetines, aceite de motor y un televisor bajo un mismo techo es alta variedad.

segments.src: 2. **Assortment** — how *deep* it goes inside one category. Also called depth. Forty running shoes in eleven widths is high assortment.
segments.tr: 2. **Surtido** — qué tan *profundo* es dentro de una categoría. También llamado profundidad. Cuarenta zapatos para correr en once anchos es un surtido alto.

segments.src: 3. **Service level** — how much labor the store spends on you. Someone measuring your inseam is expensive; a self-checkout kiosk is not.
segments.tr: 3. **Nivel de servicio** — cuánto trabajo invierte la tienda en ti. Alguien midiendo tu largo de pantalón es caro; un quiosco de autoservicio no lo es.

segments.src: 4. **Price and margin** — what all of the above costs to run, and therefore what it costs you.
segments.tr: 4. **Precio y margen** — lo que cuesta ejecutar todo lo anterior y, por lo tanto, lo que te cuesta a ti.

segments.src: No store maxes out all four.
segments.tr: Ninguna tienda lo hace bien en los cuatro.

segments.src: That's the whole point.
segments.tr: Ese es el punto.

segments.src: Every format is a deliberate trade.
segments.tr: Todo formato es un intercambio deliberado.

segments.src: **Department store** (Macy's, Nordstrom, Dillard's, Kohl's): high variety *and* decent depth, organized into walk-through departments — apparel, beauty, home, accessories.
segments.tr: **Tienda departamental** (Macy's, Nordstrom, Dillard's, Kohl's): alta variedad *y* una profundidad decente, organizada en departamentos por los que se camina — ropa, belleza, hogar, accesorios.

segments.src: High service, high margin, slow inventory turnover.
segments.tr: Servicio alto, margen alto, rotación de inventario lenta.

segments.src: Historically the format sold the *experience* of shopping as much as the goods.
segments.tr: Históricamente el formato vendía la *experiencia* de comprar tanto como los productos.

segments.src: **The big box — supercenter and warehouse club** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): maximum variety, thin service, low price.
segments.tr: **La caja grande — supercenter y club de almacén** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): variedad máxima, servicio mínimo, precio bajo.

segments.src: A Walmart Supercenter runs roughly 180,000 square feet and stocks well over 100,000 items — general merchandise plus a full grocery.
segments.tr: Un Walmart Supercenter ocupa aproximadamente 180,000 pies cuadrados e inventaría bien más de 100,000 artículos — mercancía general más un supermercado completo.

segments.src: A warehouse club goes the opposite way on depth: Costco deliberately carries only a few thousand items, one or two brands per need, sold in bulk from pallets, funded partly by an annual membership fee (about $65 for a basic card).
segments.tr: Un club de almacén va en la dirección opuesta en profundidad: Costco deliberadamente lleva solo unos pocos miles de artículos, una o dos marcas por necesidad, vendidos a granel desde palés, financiados en parte por una cuota de membresía anual (aproximadamente $65 para una tarjeta básica).

segments.src: Fewer choices → bigger orders per item → better cost from suppliers → lower shelf price.
segments.tr: Menos opciones → pedidos más grandes por artículo → mejor costo de proveedores → precio de estante más bajo.

segments.src: **Convenience store** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): tiny variety, tiny depth, tiny footprint — typically around 2,500 square feet and a few thousand items.
segments.tr: **Tienda de conveniencia** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): variedad minúscula, profundidad minúscula, espacio minúsculo — típicamente alrededor de 2,500 pies cuadrados y unos pocos miles de artículos.

segments.src: What it actually sells is *time and proximity*.
segments.tr: Lo que realmente vende es *tiempo y proximidad*.

segments.src: There are well over 100,000 of them in the U.S., a majority attached to fuel.
segments.tr: Hay bien más de 100,000 de ellas en los EE.UU., la mayoría adjuntas a gasolina.

segments.src: Merchandise margins are high — roughly a third on in-store goods, far above a supermarket — because nobody price-shops a 90-second stop.
segments.tr: Los márgenes de mercancía son altos — aproximadamente un tercio en bienes en tienda, mucho más arriba que un supermercado — porque nadie compara precios en una parada de 90 segundos.

segments.src: **Specialty store** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): narrow variety, extreme depth.
segments.tr: **Tienda especializada** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): variedad estrecha, profundidad extrema.

segments.src: One category, done exhaustively, with staff who know it.
segments.tr: Una categoría, hecha exhaustivamente, con personal que la conoce.

segments.src: When a specialty store gets big enough to dominate a category outright, it earns the nickname **category killer**.
segments.tr: Cuando una tienda especializada se hace lo suficientemente grande como para dominar una categoría completamente, gana el apodo de **asesina de categoría**.

segments.src: Underneath all four sits one arithmetic identity that explains most retail behavior:
segments.tr: Debajo de las cuatro se encuentra una identidad aritmética que explica la mayoría del comportamiento minorista:

segments.src: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover
segments.tr: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover

segments.src: You can win on fat margins and slow-moving goods (Nordstrom), or thin margins and goods that fly off the shelf (Costco, supermarkets).
segments.tr: Puedes ganar con márgenes gruesos y bienes de movimiento lento (Nordstrom), o márgenes delgados y bienes que vuelan de los estantes (Costco, supermercados).

segments.src: What you cannot do is run thin margins on slow inventory.
segments.tr: Lo que no puedes hacer es ejecutar márgenes delgados en inventario lento.

segments.src: That combination is how chains die.
segments.tr: Esa combinación es cómo mueren las cadenas.

segments.src: One honest caveat: the boundaries leak.
segments.tr: Una advertencia honesta: los límites se filtran.

segments.src: Drugstores sell milk, supermarkets sell flowers, and c-stores sell hot pizza.
segments.tr: Las farmacias venden leche, los supermercados venden flores y las tiendas de conveniencia venden pizza caliente.

segments.src: The industry term for it is **scrambled merchandising** — formats grabbing categories outside their original lane in pursuit of turnover.
segments.tr: El término de la industria para esto es **comercialización desordenada** — formatos que toman categorías fuera de su carril original en busca de rotación.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Follow one gallon of milk through a normal American week.
segments.tr: Sigue un galón de leche durante una semana americana normal.

segments.src: **Monday, 7:10 a.m.** You're already late.
segments.tr: **Lunes, 7:10 a.m.** Ya estás tarde.

segments.src: You pull into the Circle K by the interstate ramp, grab coffee and a gallon, and you're back in the car in four minutes.
segments.tr: Te metes en la Circle K junto a la rampa interestatal, agarras café y un galón, y estás de vuelta en el auto en cuatro minutos.

segments.src: Say it rings up around $5.29.
segments.tr: Digamos que suena alrededor de $5.29.

segments.src: You didn't compare anything.
segments.tr: No comparaste nada.

segments.src: You paid for the store being ninety seconds off your route and for a clerk being awake at 7 a.m.
segments.tr: Pagaste por la tienda estando noventa segundos fuera de tu ruta y por un empleado estando despierto a las 7 a.m.

segments.src: **Saturday, 10 a.m.** Costco.
segments.tr: **Sábado, 10 a.m.** Costco.

segments.src: Two gallons banded together for roughly what one and a half cost on Monday, plus the $65 membership you already sank in January.
segments.tr: Dos galones agrupados juntos por aproximadamente lo que cuesta uno y medio el lunes, más la membresía de $65 que ya invertiste en enero.

segments.src: You walked past pallets, there were maybe two brands of milk, and you bagged nothing.
segments.tr: Caminaste pasando palés, había tal vez dos marcas de leche, y no embolsaste nada.

segments.src: That's depth traded away for price.
segments.tr: Esa es la profundidad intercambiada por precio.

segments.src: **Saturday, 11:30 a.m.** Target, because you also need socks, a floor lamp, a birthday card, and a prescription.
segments.tr: **Sábado, 11:30 a.m.** Target, porque también necesitas calcetines, una lámpara de piso, una tarjeta de cumpleaños y una receta.

segments.src: Milk here is somewhere between the other two.
segments.tr: La leche aquí está en algún lugar entre los otros dos.

segments.src: You're not buying the cheapest milk — you're buying **one stop**.
segments.tr: No estás comprando la leche más barata — estás comprando **una parada**.

segments.src: Variety is the product.
segments.tr: La variedad es el producto.

segments.src: **Sunday afternoon.** Your cousin's wedding is in three weeks and you need a suit that fits.
segments.tr: **Domingo por la tarde.** La boda de tu primo es en tres semanas y necesitas un traje que te quede bien.

segments.src: You go to Nordstrom, a person puts a tape measure on you, marks the hem, and the store holds the jacket for a week.
segments.tr: Vas a Nordstrom, una persona te pone una cinta métrica, marca el dobladillo y la tienda guarda la chaqueta por una semana.

segments.src: Nobody at Costco is doing that.
segments.tr: Nadie en Costco está haciendo eso.

segments.src: You will pay for it in the price, and the store will hold that jacket in inventory for months before selling it.
segments.tr: Lo pagarás en el precio, y la tienda mantendrá esa chaqueta en inventario durante meses antes de venderla.

segments.src: **Tuesday evening.** You want *good* trail runners.
segments.tr: **Martes por la noche.** Quieres *buenos* zapatos para trail running.

segments.src: Not "shoes" — trail runners, for a specific arch.
segments.tr: No "zapatos" — zapatos para trail running, para un arco específico.

segments.src: You go to a running specialty shop or REI, where one category fills the whole store and the person on the floor asks how many miles a week you run.
segments.tr: Vas a una tienda especializada en correr o a REI, donde una categoría llena toda la tienda y la persona en el piso te pregunta cuántas millas a la semana corres.

segments.src: Five errands, five formats, and every one of them was the right choice for the mission it served.
segments.tr: Cinco recados, cinco formatos, y cada uno de ellos fue la opción correcta para la misión que sirvió.

segments.src: Buying the suit at Costco or the emergency milk at Nordstrom would both be errors — the same kind of error, in opposite directions.
segments.tr: Comprar el traje en Costco o la leche de emergencia en Nordstrom serían ambos errores — el mismo tipo de error, en direcciones opuestas.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de Tres Líneas

segments.src: 1. A retail format is a bundle of four decisions — variety, assortment, service, and price — and no format wins on all four at once.
segments.tr: 1. Un formato minorista es un conjunto de cuatro decisiones — variedad, surtido, servicio y precio — y ningún formato gana en los cuatro a la vez.

segments.src: 2. Department stores buy you breadth plus service, big boxes buy you breadth plus price, convenience stores buy you time, specialty stores buy you depth and expertise.
segments.tr: 2. Las tiendas departamentales te compran amplitud más servicio, las cajas grandes te compran amplitud más precio, las tiendas de conveniencia te compran tiempo, las tiendas especializadas te compran profundidad y experiencia.

segments.src: 3. Every one of them survives on the same equation — margin times turnover — and formats constantly poach categories from each other to keep the turnover side up.
segments.tr: 3. Cada uno de ellos sobrevive con la misma ecuación — margen por rotación — y los formatos constantemente toman categorías unos de otros para mantener el lado de la rotación arriba.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.tr: **P1.** En minorismo, "surtido" se refiere a cuál de los siguientes?

segments.tr: - (a) El número total de diferentes categorías de productos que vende una tienda

segments.src: - (b) The depth of choices offered within a single category
segments.tr: - (b) La profundidad de opciones ofrecidas dentro de una sola categoría

segments.src: - (c) The store's square footage
segments.tr: - (c) El metraje cuadrado de la tienda

segments.tr: **P2.** Costco lleva solo unos pocos miles de artículos mientras que un Walmart Supercenter lleva bien más de 100,000.

segments.src: This mainly reflects a difference in strategy, not a failure by Costco.
segments.tr: Esto principalmente refleja una diferencia en la estrategia, no un fracaso de Costco.

segments.src: (O / X)
segments.tr: (V / F)

segments.src: **Q3.** A convenience store charges more for the same gallon of milk than a supermarket does primarily because:
segments.tr: **P3.** Una tienda de conveniencia cobra más por el mismo galón de leche que un supermercado principalmente porque:

segments.src: - (a) Its milk is a higher grade of product
segments.tr: - (a) Su leche es un producto de mayor calidad

segments.src: - (b) It is legally required to price above supermarkets
segments.tr: - (b) Se requiere legalmente que fije precios por encima de los supermercados

segments.tr: - (c) Sus clientes compran proximidad y velocidad, y su pequeña escala conlleva un costo más alto por artículo vendido

segments.src: - (d) It buys milk from different farms
segments.tr: - (d) Compra leche de granjas diferentes

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **Retail format** — the recurring combination of variety, assortment, service level, and price that defines a type of store.
segments.tr: - **Formato minorista** — la combinación recurrente de variedad, surtido, nivel de servicio y precio que define un tipo de tienda.

segments.src: - **Variety (breadth)** — how many distinct product categories a retailer carries.
segments.tr: - **Variedad (amplitud)** — cuántas categorías de productos distintas vende un minorista.

segments.src: - **Assortment (depth)** — how many choices — brands, sizes, styles — a retailer offers inside one category.
segments.tr: - **Surtido (profundidad)** — cuántas opciones — marcas, tamaños, estilos — ofrece un minorista dentro de una categoría.

segments.src: - **Scrambled merchandising** — a retailer adding categories outside its traditional lane, which blurs the lines between formats.
segments.tr: - **Comercialización desordenada** — un minorista agregando categorías fuera de su carril tradicional, lo que difumina las líneas entre formatos.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — how many times a year a retailer sells through and replaces its stock; the counterweight to gross margin.
segments.tr: - **Rotación de inventario** — cuántas veces al año un minorista vende y reemplaza su existencia; el contrapeso al margen bruto.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** Assortment is depth within a category; breadth across categories is "variety."
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **P1 — (b).** Surtido es profundidad dentro de una categoría; amplitud entre categorías es "variedad."

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Costco's limited item count is the mechanism of its low prices: fewer SKUs means larger orders per item, better supplier costs, and simpler operations.
segments.tr: **P2 — V.** El conteo limitado de artículos de Costco es el mecanismo de sus precios bajos: menos SKU significa pedidos más grandes por artículo, costos de proveedores mejor y operaciones más simples.

segments.src: **Q3 — (c).** The milk is the same product.
segments.tr: **P3 — (c).** La leche es el mismo producto.

segments.src: You are paying for location, hours, and speed, plus the higher per-item cost of running a 2,500-square-foot store — which is why in-store merchandise margins at convenience stores run far above supermarket levels.*
segments.tr: Estás pagando por ubicación, horarios y velocidad, más el costo más alto por artículo de operar una tienda de 2,500 pies cuadrados — que es por qué los márgenes de mercancía en tienda en tiendas de conveniencia se ejecutan muy por encima de los niveles de supermercado.*

segments.tr: خدمة عالية وهامش عالي ودوران بطيء للمخزون.

segments.src: Historically the format sold the *experience* of shopping as much as the goods.
segments.tr: تاريخيًا، باعت الصيغة *تجربة* التسوق بقدر ما باعت السلع.

segments.src: **The big box — supercenter and warehouse club** (Walmart Supercenter, Target, Meijer; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's): maximum variety, thin service, low price.
segments.tr: **متجر البضائع الضخم — فائق السعر ومستودع النادي** (Walmart Supercenter و Target و Meijer؛ Costco و Sam's Club و BJ's): أقصى تنوع وخدمة رقيقة وسعر منخفض.

segments.src: A Walmart Supercenter runs roughly 180,000 square feet and stocks well over 100,000 items — general merchandise plus a full grocery.
segments.tr: يعمل Walmart Supercenter تقريبًا على 180000 قدم مربع ويحتفظ بأكثر من 100000 عنصر — سلع عامة بالإضافة إلى بقالة كاملة.

segments.src: A warehouse club goes the opposite way on depth: Costco deliberately carries only a few thousand items, one or two brands per need, sold in bulk from pallets, funded partly by an annual membership fee (about $65 for a basic card).
segments.tr: يذهب نادي المستودع بالطريقة المعاكسة على العمق: Costco يحمل عن قصد فقط بضعة آلاف من العناصر وعلامة تجارية واحدة أو اثنتان لكل احتياجات مبيعة بكميات كبيرة من المنصات، ممولة جزئيًا برسم عضوية سنوي (حوالي 65 دولارًا لبطاقة أساسية).

segments.src: Fewer choices → bigger orders per item → better cost from suppliers → lower shelf price.
segments.tr: خيارات أقل → طلبات أكبر لكل عنصر → تكاليف أفضل من الموردين → سعر رف أقل.

segments.src: **Convenience store** (7-Eleven, Wawa, QuikTrip, Circle K): tiny variety, tiny depth, tiny footprint — typically around 2,500 square feet and a few thousand items.
segments.tr: **متجر المتاجر المريحة** (7-Eleven و Wawa و QuikTrip و Circle K): تنوع صغير وعمق صغير وبصمة صغيرة — عادة حوالي 2500 قدم مربع وبضعة آلاف من العناصر.

segments.src: What it actually sells is *time and proximity*.
segments.tr: ما يبيعه في الواقع هو *الوقت والقرب*.

segments.src: There are well over 100,000 of them in the U.S., a majority attached to fuel.
segments.tr: هناك أكثر من 100000 منهم في الولايات المتحدة ومعظمهم متصل بالوقود.

segments.src: Merchandise margins are high — roughly a third on in-store goods, far above a supermarket — because nobody price-shops a 90-second stop.
segments.tr: هوامش البضائع عالية — حوالي الثلث على البضائع المتعلقة بالمتجر، بعيد جدًا عن السوبر ماركت — لأن لا أحد يقارن أسعار محطة 90 ثانية.

segments.src: **Specialty store** (Sephora, Foot Locker, REI, Best Buy, Home Depot): narrow variety, extreme depth.
segments.tr: **متجر متخصص** (Sephora و Foot Locker و REI و Best Buy و Home Depot): تنوع ضيق وعمق متطرف.

segments.src: One category, done exhaustively, with staff who know it.
segments.tr: فئة واحدة مع الكثير من الاستنزاف وموظفين يعرفونها.

segments.src: When a specialty store gets big enough to dominate a category outright, it earns the nickname **category killer**.
segments.tr: عندما يصبح متجر متخصص كبيرًا بدرجة كافية ليهيمن على فئة ما تمامًا، فإنه يكسب لقب **category killer**.

segments.src: Underneath all four sits one arithmetic identity that explains most retail behavior:
segments.tr: تحت الأربعة جميعًا توجد هوية حسابية واحدة تشرح معظم سلوك التجزئة:

segments.src: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover
segments.tr: retail profit engine = gross margin × inventory turnover

segments.src: You can win on fat margins and slow-moving goods (Nordstrom), or thin margins and goods that fly off the shelf (Costco, supermarkets).
segments.tr: يمكنك الفوز برسوم سمينة والسلع البطيئة الحركة (Nordstrom) أو الهوامش الرقيقة والسلع التي تطير من على الرف (Costco والأسواق الكبرى).

segments.src: What you cannot do is run thin margins on slow inventory.
segments.tr: ما لا يمكنك فعله هو تشغيل هوامش رقيقة على مخزون بطيء.

segments.src: That combination is how chains die.
segments.tr: هذا المزيج هو كيف تموت السلاسل.

segments.src: One honest caveat: the boundaries leak.
segments.tr: حذر واحد صادق: تسرب الحدود.

segments.src: Drugstores sell milk, supermarkets sell flowers, and c-stores sell hot pizza.
segments.tr: تبيع الصيدليات الحليب والسوبر ماركت تبيع الزهور والمتاجر c- تبيع البيتزا الساخنة.

segments.src: The industry term for it is **scrambled merchandising** — formats grabbing categories outside their original lane in pursuit of turnover.
segments.tr: المصطلح الصناعي له هو **scrambled merchandising** — صيغ تستهدف الفئات خارج مسارها الأصلي في السعي وراء الدوران.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Follow one gallon of milk through a normal American week.
segments.tr: اتبع جالونًا من الحليب خلال أسبوع أمريكي طبيعي.

segments.src: **Monday, 7:10 a.m.** You're already late.
segments.tr: **الاثنين 7:10 صباحًا** أنت متأخر بالفعل.

segments.src: You pull into the Circle K by the interstate ramp, grab coffee and a gallon, and you're back in the car in four minutes.
segments.tr: تسحب إلى Circle K بجانب منحدر الطريق السريع، وتلتقط القهوة والجالون وتعود إلى السيارة في أربع دقائق.

segments.src: Say it rings up around $5.29.
segments.tr: قل أنه يرن حوالي 5.29 دولار.

segments.src: You didn't compare anything.
segments.tr: لم تقارن أي شيء.

segments.src: You paid for the store being ninety seconds off your route and for a clerk being awake at 7 a.m.
segments.tr: دفعت للمتجر كونه تسعين ثانية خارج طريقك ولموظف يستيقظ في الساعة 7 صباحًا.

segments.src: **Saturday, 10 a.m.** Costco.
segments.tr: **السبت 10 صباحًا** Costco.

segments.src: Two gallons banded together for roughly what one and a half cost on Monday, plus the $65 membership you already sank in January.
segments.tr: جالونين مرتبطين معاً لتقريباً ما يكلف واحد ونصف يوم الاثنين، بالإضافة إلى 65 دولار العضوية التي غطست بالفعل في يناير.

segments.src: You walked past pallets, there were maybe two brands of milk, and you bagged nothing.
segments.tr: مشيت بجانب المنصات، وربما كان هناك ماركتان فقط من الحليب، ولم تضع شيئًا.

segments.src: That's depth traded away for price.
segments.tr: هذا هو العمق الذي تم تبديله مقابل السعر.

segments.src: **Saturday, 11:30 a.m.** Target, because you also need socks, a floor lamp, a birthday card, and a prescription.
segments.tr: **السبت 11:30 صباحًا** Target لأنك تحتاج أيضًا إلى جوارب ومصباح أرضي وبطاقة عيد ميلاد والتزام طبي.

segments.src: Milk here is somewhere between the other two.
segments.tr: الحليب هنا بين الاثنين الآخرين.

segments.src: You're not buying the cheapest milk — you're buying **one stop**.
segments.tr: أنت لا تشتري أرخص حليب — أنت تشتري **محطة واحدة**.

segments.src: Variety is the product.
segments.tr: التنوع هو المنتج.

segments.src: **Sunday afternoon.** Your cousin's wedding is in three weeks and you need a suit that fits.
segments.tr: **الأحد بعد الظهر.** زفاف ابن عم لك في ثلاثة أسابيع وتحتاج إلى بدلة تناسب.

segments.src: You go to Nordstrom, a person puts a tape measure on you, marks the hem, and the store holds the jacket for a week.
segments.tr: تذهب إلى Nordstrom، وشخص يضع شريط قياس عليك ويضع علامة على الهيم، والمتجر يحمل السترة لمدة أسبوع.

segments.src: Nobody at Costco is doing that.
segments.tr: لا أحد في Costco يفعل ذلك.

segments.src: You will pay for it in the price, and the store will hold that jacket in inventory for months before selling it.
segments.tr: ستدفع مقابل ذلك في السعر والمتجر سيحتفظ بتلك السترة في المخزون لأشهر قبل بيعها.

segments.src: **Tuesday evening.** You want *good* trail runners.
segments.tr: **الثلاثاء مساء.** تريد *جيد* متسابق درب.

segments.src: Not "shoes" — trail runners, for a specific arch.
segments.tr: ليس "أحذية" — متسابقو درب لقوس محدد.

segments.src: You go to a running specialty shop or REI, where one category fills the whole store and the person on the floor asks how many miles a week you run.
segments.tr: تذهب إلى متجر متخصص في الجري أو REI حيث تملأ فئة واحدة المتجر بالكامل والشخص على الأرض يسأل كم عدد الأميال التي تركضها في الأسبوع.

segments.src: Five errands, five formats, and every one of them was the right choice for the mission it served.
segments.tr: خمسة مهام خمس صيغ وكل واحد منهم كان الخيار الصحيح للمهمة التي خدمها.

segments.src: Buying the suit at Costco or the emergency milk at Nordstrom would both be errors — the same kind of error, in opposite directions.
segments.tr: شراء البدلة في Costco أو حليب الطوارئ في Nordstrom كلاهما سيكون أخطاء — نفس النوع من الخطأ في اتجاهات معاكسة.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص بثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. A retail format is a bundle of four decisions — variety, assortment, service, and price — and no format wins on all four at once.
segments.tr: 1. صيغة البيع بالتجزئة هي حزمة من أربعة قرارات — التنوع والتشكيلة والخدمة والسعر — ولا صيغة تفوز على الأربعة في آن واحد.

segments.src: 2. Department stores buy you breadth plus service, big boxes buy you breadth plus price, convenience stores buy you time, specialty stores buy you depth and expertise.
segments.tr: 2. متاجر المتاجر الكبرى تشتري لك العرض والخدمة والصناديق الكبرى تشتري لك العرض والسعر ومتاجر المتاجر المريحة تشتري لك الوقت ومتاجر متخصصة تشتري لك العمق والخبرة.

segments.src: 3. Every one of them survives on the same equation — margin times turnover — and formats constantly poach categories from each other to keep the turnover side up.
segments.tr: 3. كل واحد منهم يبقى على نفس المعادلة — الهامش مرات الدوران — والصيغ الطاعم باستمرار فئات من بعضهم البعض للحفاظ على جانب الدوران.

segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: - (a) العدد الإجمالي للفئات المختلفة من المنتجات التي يحملها المتجر

segments.tr: **Q2.** تحمل Costco فقط بضعة آلاف من العناصر بينما يحمل Walmart Supercenter أكثر من 100000.

segments.tr: هذا يعكس في الغالب اختلافًا في الإستراتيجية وليس فشل من قبل Costco.

segments.tr: **Q3.** يفرض متجر المتاجر المريحة رسومًا أعلى لنفس جالون الحليب من سوبر ماركت بشكل أساسي لأن:

segments.src: - (a) Its milk is a higher grade of product
segments.tr: - (a) حليبه هو منتج من الدرجة الأعلى

segments.tr: - (b) يُطلب منه قانونًا تسعير الحد الأدنى فوق السوبر ماركت
